script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for May 9. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

Clean water, sewage systems, handwashing—these boring basics have saved more lives than all the dramatic medical breakthroughs combined.  Before we understood germs, cities were death traps.  Sanitation made modern civilization possible.

Separating drinking water from sewage was transformative. London's cholera epidemics ended when contaminated pumps were identified and clean water supplied. Simple infrastructure—pipes and processing—made cities livable. In the 1840s, Ignaz Semmelweis showed that doctors washing hands between patients dramatically reduced deaths.  He was ignored and ridiculed.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Prevention is more powerful than cure.  Sanitation teaches that stopping problems before they start beats fixing them after.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Sanitation Gratitude - Notice the Systems.

Here's your activity: Notice the sanitation systems you use without thinking: clean tap water, sewage that disappears, refrigeration preserving food. Each represents centuries of learning about disease prevention. What would life be like without them? This helps you appreciate invisible sanitation infrastructure.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about why clean matters can be applied to sanitation gratitude - notice the systems. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
